title: Analytical concepts
description: How a dataset is analytically shaped, independent of its theme. The same five nodes the ontology explorer already draws, but with stable IDs, written definitions and explicit assignment rules instead of a title regex.

concepts.definition: A measured or modelled value describing conditions at a point in time, including composite indices. Answers 'what is it like'.
concepts.note: Assign when the dataset carries a quantity or index for a single period.

concepts.definition: A trend, dynamic or difference between periods. Answers 'what changed'. Takes precedence over a state observation when both readings are possible.
concepts.note: Requires a temporalCoverage interval spanning more than one year, or an explicit dynamics/trend/change term in the source title.

concepts.definition: A hazard, the exposure of people or assets to it, or its recorded losses. Answers 'what could go wrong and who is affected'.
concepts.note: Hazard evidence outranks the presence of a year range, so an event catalogue spanning decades stays a hazard dataset.

concepts.definition: A managed system with infrastructure, allocation or service delivery: irrigation, drainage, canals, water and sanitation access, farming systems, protected-area management.
concepts.note: Assign when the subject is human management of a resource rather than the resource's physical state.

concepts.definition: A mapped entity or classification with a fixed footprint: landscapes, ecoregions, climate types, geomorphology, plant formations. Answers 'what is where'.
concepts.note: Default when no other concept has supporting evidence.
